variables.name: matrixSummary
variables.value: The refined Stage 3 analysis matrix establishes a rigorous, evidence-grounded framework across five distinct analytical questions (Q1 to Q5) and four non-overlapping analytical perspectives: the User, People Discussed, Interactions, and ChatGPT. Rather than conflating conversation text into generic summaries, each question operates with explicit methodological boundaries: Q1 focuses on user goals and unfinished technical/creative projects outside relationship topics; Q2 examines turn-by-turn user directives and assistant adaptations; Q3 isolates assistant-introduced premises, hallucinations, and unverified assumptions to prevent model echo; Q4 reconstructs the chronological evolution of ChatGPT usage across three verified operational periods spanning August 25, 2024 through August 5, 2026, while explicitly identifying the post-August 5, 2026 to October 2026 boundary gap; and Q5 addresses interpersonal interactions using a strict four-layer provenance model (direct third-party quotes, user event reports, user subjective reactions, and assistant diagnostic interpretations) that categorically prohibits clinical diagnosis and treats diagnostic labels (such as BPD) strictly as reported narrative terms with traceable provenance.

value.question: Which substantive topics, unfinished projects, and technical investigations outside relationship material merit resumption, and what precise context is needed to continue them?
value.subject: Substantive technical projects, workflows, operational designs, and creative investigations outside relationship material
value.perspective: User goals, project lifecycles, and practical continuation
value.method: Filter candidate clusters to exclude personal relationship discussions; traverse branch histories along individual conversation DAGs to extract initial problem statements, technical constraints, generated artifacts, stopping nodes, and unfulfilled next steps; formulate actionable resumption prompts.
value.evidenceRequirements: Mandatory citation fields: source_file, source_record_index, conversation_id, mapping node_id, message_id, and message.create_time. Requires verification that stopping points are evidenced in source turn text, accompanied by cross-conversation contradiction checks to verify the project was not completed in a later thread.

variables.name: designSummary
variables.value: The Stage 3 passage boundary specification establishes a four-tier structural hierarchy: Conversation -> Branch Path -> Ordered Turn Exchange -> Classification Passage. Natural conversation trees are decomposed into distinct, non-concatenated branch paths by following explicit parent-child pointer chains in the conversation mapping graph. Each branch path is partitioned into discrete turn exchanges (User prompt -> Assistant response, capturing intermediate tool operations). To ensure interpretive clarity without label contamination, every classification passage strictly delineates the active target exchange (the sole locus of label assignment and evidentiary quotation) from contextual framing (`contextBefore` for antecedent constraints and pronoun resolution; `contextAfter` for subsequent user corrections and reaction tracking). Overlap between sliding windows is tracked deterministically through explicit target node identifiers, preventing repeated context turns from inflating empirical evidence counts during synthesis.

value.exchangeDefinition: An exchange unit is an ordered bipartite or tripartite turn sequence within an isolated conversation branch: commencing with a user prompt node (`message.author.role == 'user'`), traversing any immediate tool invocation or system intermediary nodes, and terminating at the corresponding assistant response node (`message.author.role == 'assistant'`). Null-message structural nodes are bypassed by following direct edge pointers.
value.targetDelineation: The target passage is the primary evaluative unit consisting strictly of the designated core exchange. Semantic labels (subject/topic, user purpose, analytical perspective, conversation outcome) must be assigned solely based on text within the target passage. All label-supporting citations must reference message IDs, node IDs, and character offsets located exclusively within this target boundary.
value.contextBeforeRules: Preceding context (`contextBefore`) encompasses up to N antecedent exchanges along the exact directed ancestry chain (`node.parent`). It provides necessary referential grounding, pronoun resolution, and background constraint awareness. Topics, requests, or entities appearing exclusively within `contextBefore` must not contribute labels or primary evidence counts to the target unit.
value.contextAfterRules: Subsequent context (`contextAfter`) encompasses up to M descendant exchanges following the target's terminal node along the designated active branch. It provides visibility into user reactions, corrections, or follow-ups to evaluate conversation outcomes. Post-target shifts or subsequent inquiries occurring in `contextAfter` must never back-propagate to label the target unit.
value.branchPreservationRules: Conversation tree structures must be traversed from root to leaf via parent-to-child links. Every fork point (`children.length > 1`) generates distinct, isolated branch paths. Alternative sibling replies are never concatenated or interleaved into a synthetic linear sequence. Each branch path maintains its own independent exchange sequence indexed by branch and node ancestry.
value.overlapTrackingMechanism: Each prepared passage is indexed by a deterministic composite key (`targetPassageId`) and explicitly lists its constituent `targetNodeIds` separately from `contextNodeIds`. Evidence indexing, topic frequency aggregations, and perspective synthesis algorithms must filter strictly on `targetNodeIds`, ensuring that passages sharing context windows never produce duplicate evidentiary weight.

value.sizeWindow: 1 User Prompt + 1 Assistant Response (typically 200–800 tokens; 2 conversational turns)
value.rationale: Isolates the immediate functional request and response to measure whether topic discovery and classification can operate at minimal conversational granularity without noise from adjacent topics.
value.advantages: Eliminates intra-passage topic mixing; provides pinpoint citation accuracy and unambiguous speaker attribution; creates clean mapping boundaries that prevent adjacent discussion drift.
value.potentialRisks: Higher vulnerability to contextual insufficiency on short, elliptic, or anaphoric follow-up prompts (e.g., 'why?', 'continue', or pronoun-heavy responses), requiring frequent fallback to contextBefore.

value.sizeWindow: 3 Sequential Exchanges: Target centered between 1 preceding and 1 succeeding exchange (~1,200–3,500 tokens; 6 conversational turns)
value.rationale: Balances immediate request-reply mechanics with local conversational momentum, capturing immediate clarifications, corrections, and multi-turn explanations within a manageable context window.
value.advantages: High contextual sufficiency for iterative tasks, software debugging, and multi-step reasoning; directly captures correction loops (Q2) and immediate assistant assumptions (Q3) in a unified window.
value.potentialRisks: Moderate risk of topic mixing across abrupt conversational pivots; requires strict enforcement to ensure workers do not label background turns as target evidence.

value.sizeWindow: Variable Window of 5 to 10 Sequential Exchanges bounded by detected topic shifts or session pauses (up to 8,000 tokens; 10–20 turns)
value.rationale: Evaluates whether macro-level user trajectories, protracted project designs, or extended relationship reflections can be captured holistically as unified episodes.
value.advantages: Maximizes contextual sufficiency and thematic coherence for long-horizon goals (Q1) and chronological usage analysis (Q4); avoids artificial fragmentation of extended workflows.
value.potentialRisks: Severe topic dilution and keyword mixing; citations become coarse or ambiguous across long transcripts; high risk of conflating distinct conversational shifts into a single generic label.

- Message content and author: message.id, message.author.role, message.create_time, message.content.parts
- Metadata and citation references: metadata, attachments, asset_pointer, file_name, mime_type, size_bytes, source, source_title, source_url, source_type, sources, metadata_sources, content_references

Review `project/stage3-pilot/analysis-matrix.json`, `project/stage3-pilot/REPORT.md`, `project/README.md`, and `project/CHECKLIST.md`.

The current analysis matrix proposes five analytical questions (Q1 to Q5) with provisional priorities. You must refine and formalize this matrix:
1. Refine the five analytical questions: Q1 (revisit candidate topics/projects), Q2 (user requests and corrections), Q3 (assistant assumptions and influence), Q4 (dated evolution of ChatGPT usage), and Q5 (people discussed, attribution, and interactions).
2. For each question, establish:
   - Precise analytical subject and perspective (User, People Discussed, Interactions, ChatGPT).
   - Answerable method tailored to conversation text.
   - Evidence requirements (mandatory citation fields, contradiction checks, distinguishing reports from direct actions).
   - Specific analytical limitations (e.g., absence of attachment bytes, inability to diagnose, lack of external ground truth).
   - Concrete intended output specification.
3. Establish operational comparison periods based on the observed archive range (August 25, 2024 to August 5, 2026), defining distinct chronological periods and explicitly identifying the boundary where October 2026 data is absent.
4. Write the resulting refined matrix to `project/stage3-pilot/refined-analysis-matrix.json`.

You must design the natural conversation-to-exchange-to-classification-passage subdivision specification for Stage 3:
1. Unit hierarchy: Define structural unit transitions (Conversation -> Branch Path -> Ordered Turn Exchange -> Classification Passage).
2. Target vs Context: Formulate strict boundary rules defining the target passage (labeled unit) versus `contextBefore` and `contextAfter` (interpretive context that must not contribute labels to the target).

# Conversation Archive Analysis

## Execution checklist

See [CHECKLIST.md](CHECKLIST.md) for the ordered requirements, dependencies, and parallelization plan. **The Gemini parallelizer is complete and live-tested.** Archive preparation and analysis remain outstanding.

## Purpose and current scope

Preserve the user's goals and the analysis-design questions discussed on October 15, 2026, so this project can be resumed without reconstructing the conversation.

The eventual task is to analyze a large ChatGPT conversation export containing multiple topics and perspectives. The immediate task is to design an appropriate analysis: determine which questions to ask, what methods and tools can answer them, and how to process the archive thoroughly without losing context.

This folder is a sibling of AGENTS Procedure under ChatMachines/Workflow Interactive Procedures. It is a separate project, not a modification of that procedure.

This README records goals and proposed methods. The archive has not been inspected for this project; no findings, date coverage, diagnoses, or completeness claims have been established.

## Procedure for the analysis

Use the existing AGENTS Procedure to carry out this archive analysis. Follow its README to start and complete the interactive run, supply the values requested by each rendered instruction, and let the existing workflow control transitions.

Location: `ChatMachines/Workflow Interactive Procedures/AGENTS Procedure/`

[AGENTS Procedure folder](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/tree/main/ChatMachines/Workflow%20Interactive%20Procedures/AGENTS%20Procedure)

[AGENTS Procedure README](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/blob/main/ChatMachines/Workflow%20Interactive%20Procedures/AGENTS%20Procedure/README.md)

## Source archive

User-provided Library reference:

https://chatgpt.com/library/share/libfile_8eeefed45af881919c1fdb5c15604019?account_id=personal

Library identifier: libfile_8eeefed45af881919c1fdb5c15604019

Retrieve the actual file through authenticated Library access when beginning analysis. Establish its filename, format, version, size, date range, conversation structure, attachments, and completeness from the retrieved source. Do not assume this link identifies a particular export format or that it contains all account history.

Do not copy the private archive, quoted personal messages, or sensitive analysis into this repository merely because this README is here. Decide appropriate storage when the analysis begins; the current request authorizes preserving the project outline.

## Goals

1. Determine how to analyze the archive before selecting a single analytical lens.
2. Understand the questions the user was trying to resolve, how their thinking changed, and whether the conversations helped.
3. Examine relationship material from distinct perspectives: the user, the person discussed, their interactions, and ChatGPT's contributions.
4. Explore material outside relationship discussions. Rediscover interesting topics, promising ideas, unfinished projects, and investigations worth resuming.
5. Trace how the user's use of ChatGPT changed from 2024–2025 to the present, while identifying continuities and exceptions.
6. Produce useful questions, prompts, methods, and outputs for further investigation rather than assuming the right analysis is already known.
7. Make coverage, evidence, limitations, and remaining work explicit.

## Core question

How should this ChatGPT conversation archive be analyzed to understand what the user was trying to resolve, how their thinking changed, whether the analysis helped, what substantive topics merit revisiting, and how their use of ChatGPT evolved?

First inspect the archive's structure and representative conversations. Do not assume every topic needs the same analysis or that one method answers every question.

## Subproblems

| Subproblem | Decision or output needed |
| --- | --- |
| Goals and questions | Identify and prioritize answerable questions and the decisions they would inform. |
| Archive preparation | Parse the actual export, retain original text, account for conversations, messages, attachments, dates, branches, and errors. |
| Inventory | Record conversation IDs, dates, titles, message counts, lengths, and available metadata. Give messages stable references. |
| Subdivision | Choose chunk boundaries, sizes, overlap, and links between related parts without losing meaning. |
| Topic mapping | Identify subjects, recurring concerns, related conversations, and discussions that cross topic boundaries. |
| People and attribution | Identify speakers and people discussed; distinguish direct messages, quotations, user reports, and model-generated interpretations. |
| Perspectives | Separate analysis of the user, other people, interactions, and ChatGPT's behavior and influence. |
| Chronology | Reconstruct event and discussion sequences; distinguish when something happened from when it was discussed. |
| Evidence quality | Assess support, contradictions, ambiguity, missing context, and dependence between repeated claims. |
| Method selection | Choose an appropriate method for each question and explain its limitations. |
| Cross-part synthesis | Connect findings across chunks, topics, and periods without flattening differences or losing source references. |
| Verification | Check parsing completeness, coverage, citations, contradictory evidence, and whether questions were actually answered. |
| Deliverables | Choose useful timelines, topic catalogs, evidence-linked findings, unresolved questions, and prompts for continuing work. |
| Recovery and continuation | Save analysis progress and decisions so later work can resume without repeating completed processing. |

These are an initial decomposition. Inspect the archive for additional necessary subproblems and document them.

## Analytical perspectives

### The user

Examine expressed concerns, assumptions, emotions, interpretations, decisions, recurring questions, and changes over time. Distinguish explicit statements from inferred motives. Avoid treating an inference as a settled fact about the user.

### People discussed

Examine documented or reported behavior. Distinguish their direct words from the user's descriptions and ChatGPT's interpretations. An archive of discussions about someone does not provide unrestricted access to that person's motives or mental state.

The user has referred to a girlfriend with borderline personality disorder. Establish the source and status of any diagnostic label; do not assume the label explains behavior or independently diagnose someone from the archive.

### Relationships and interactions

Examine recurring sequences, conflict, boundaries, responses, repair attempts, decisions, and changes in interactions. Consider alternative explanations and evidence inconsistent with a proposed pattern.

### ChatGPT

Examine advice, interpretations, assumptions, contradictions, corrections, and possible influence on subsequent conversations. Distinguish an independently supported claim from an interpretation the model introduced and later conversations repeated.

Do not force every topic through every perspective. Select perspectives according to the question and available evidence.

## Topics worth revisiting

Build a navigable catalog of substantive topics beyond relationship material. For each candidate, preserve:

- Topic and the questions originally explored.
- Why it may be interesting or useful to revisit.
- Relevant conversation and message references.
- What was concluded, attempted, produced, or left unresolved.
- Where the discussion stopped and what context is needed to resume.
- A useful next question or prompt.

Separate rediscovery from evaluation: first locate an idea, then assess whether its original premises and conclusions withstand review.

## Evolution of ChatGPT use

Compare the user's 2024–2025 use with their current use, using dated evidence. Determine available comparison periods from the source rather than presuming the archive reaches the present.

| Dimension | What to compare |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Information seeking, reflection, exploration, creation, problem solving, and execution. |
| User's role | Asking questions, collaborating, directing work, reviewing results, and designing procedures. |
| Instructions | Specificity, constraints, examples, permissions, expected outputs, and formal procedures. |
| Interaction | Follow-ups, corrections, experimentation, conversation length, and sustained projects. |
| Trust and verification | Accepting, challenging, checking, and demanding evidence for answers or completion. |
| Tools and artifacts | Files, scripts, repositories, integrations, workflows, and external services. |
| Results | Concrete outputs, achieved objectives, unresolved work, and consequences observable in the record. |

Support each claimed change with dated examples. Look for continuities and counterexamples. Distinguish changes in user behavior from changes in available models, features, tasks, or circumstances where the evidence permits. Identify missing current-period data rather than inventing a comparison.

## Managing the large-file problem

A large archive is a collection of linked records, not a single prompt to be compressed into one model context.

1. Preserve the original source and establish its identity and version.
2. Use scripts to extract structure and build an inventory with stable references.
3. Map topics and questions. A topic map locates evidence; it does not replace reading it.
4. Select and document a subdivision strategy before substantive interpretation.
5. Analyze bounded sections with enough surrounding context for the particular question.
6. Record findings with original message references, supporting passages, contradictory evidence, and uncertainty.
7. Synthesize across sections and return to original passages when conclusions depend on context.
8. Verify coverage and unresolved questions.

### Subdivision is its own subproblem

Keep conversations intact where practical. Split oversized conversations at meaningful boundaries, retain their original order and identifiers, and preserve links across chunks.

Choose size and overlap according to the model limits and analysis question. Chronological analysis may require different groupings from thematic analysis. Preserve branch structure when present; do not treat every export node as belonging to one linear conversation.

Verify no messages were omitted. Track intentional overlap separately so repeated material is not counted as independent evidence.

### Coverage and evidence

Maintain a coverage ledger distinguishing:

- Inventoried.
- Searched.
- Read.
- Analyzed for a named question.
- Included in synthesis.
- Verified against the original.

Searching the entire archive is not reading the entire archive. Summarizing every chunk is not proof that every analysis question has been answered.

Define completeness separately for each question. Distinguish comprehensive processing from sampled review. Do not repeatedly summarize summaries until the original evidence and exceptions disappear.

Use scripts for extraction, indexing, counts, reference integrity, and coverage accounting. Use models for interpretation with traceable evidence. Choose specific tools only after inspecting the actual format and requirements.

## Analysis matrix

Before substantive analysis, connect each proposed question to:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Question | The precise question to investigate. |
| Subject | The person, interaction, topic, or usage pattern under examination. |
| Perspective | The analytical angle appropriate to this question. |
| Material | Relevant conversations, periods, passages, and any missing sources. |
| Method | Proposed approach and why it fits. |
| Evidence requirements | What would support, contradict, or limit an answer. |
| Coverage | Whether exhaustive processing or sampling is needed, and how this will be tracked. |
| Limitations | What the archive cannot establish. |
| Output | The useful form of the result. |
| Next prompt | The concrete instruction needed to perform this part. |

## Expected initial deliverables

After source inspection, produce:

1. A factual archive inventory and a statement of missing or uncertain material.
2. A refined decomposition of the analysis problem.
3. A topic map and initial catalog of discussions worth revisiting.
4. An analysis matrix covering the user's chosen questions and perspectives.
5. A justified subdivision and coverage strategy.
6. A prioritized executable analysis plan, with prompts for its parts.
7. A progress record identifying completed work, remaining work, and decisions needed from the user.

These are future work, not artifacts already produced by this README.

## Suggested starting instruction

Retrieve the linked ChatGPT export and inspect its structure before choosing an analysis method. Determine which questions it can answer and decompose the task into the necessary subproblems.

Include archive preparation, subdivision, topic mapping, source attribution, chronology, analytical perspectives, evidence assessment, synthesis, and verification. Identify additional subproblems revealed by the source.

Create an analysis matrix connecting each question to its subject, perspective, relevant material, method, evidence requirements, limitations, coverage standard, and intended output. Keep analysis of the user, other people, their interactions, and ChatGPT's contributions distinct while examining their connections.

Include rediscovery of interesting topics and unfinished projects outside relationship material. Separately plan an evidence-based comparison of the user's 2024–2025 ChatGPT use with their present use, establishing whether sufficient material exists for each period.

Design and implement an appropriate way to subdivide the archive without losing context. Preserve stable references and verify that no messages were omitted. Track what was inventoried, searched, read, analyzed, and verified.

Recommend which questions to pursue first and write the specific prompts needed. Ground conclusions in original passages; distinguish observations, reports, interpretations, and unresolved possibilities. Do not substitute repeated claims for independent evidence or summaries for source review.

## Resuming this project

Read this README, retrieve the current source, and inspect existing project outputs before creating new work. Continue from verified saved progress. The AGENTS interactive procedure remains at ../AGENTS Procedure/README.md; use its existing mechanisms for this analysis, preserving the distinction between procedure infrastructure and this archive-analysis project.

## Parallel Gemini execution substrate

The runner is in parallel-gemini/. Its workflow is .github/workflows/conversation-parallel-gemini.yml (Conversation Parallel Gemini).

Supply an array of repository-relative file or directory paths and one shared instruction. Each path becomes an independent Gemini matrix job. Jobs run concurrently up to maxParallel (1–16, default 4); one failed job does not cancel the others. Non-hidden UTF-8 text files are read as text. PNG and JPEG file data (detected by signature, even when the extension is misleading) are sent as inline image data to Gemini; image files are processed one per request. Directory paths recurse over eligible text and image files. The worker has no fixed source-byte cap. All eligible text files for an assignment are sent together in one Gemini request, so model context, API request-size, and response limits still apply; divide work at meaningful boundaries when needed. Symlinks, other binary formats, and missing paths are rejected.

The worker uses repository secret GEMINI_API_KEY and optional repository variable GEMINI_MODEL. It calls the same generateContent endpoint and default model as the existing Gemini integration. The worker analyzes and writes results; it does not edit assigned source files, delegate recursively, subdivide an archive, or decide the analysis strategy.

Start manually in Actions → Conversation Parallel Gemini → Run workflow. Enter paths as a JSON array, instruction as text, and maxParallel as an integer. Alternatively edit and commit parallel-gemini/trigger.json to main:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "<fresh ISO timestamp>",
  "enabled": true,
  "paths": ["path/to/part-1.json", "path/to/part-2.json"],
  "instruction": "Analyze the assigned material and cite original locations.",
  "maxParallel": 2
}
```

The placeholders above must be replaced with existing repository paths. Only a commit changing the enabled trigger launches API jobs; ordinary source changes run tests. Set enabled to false to disable a trigger update. A trigger does not automatically import the Library archive. Do not commit private conversation content just to satisfy the repository-path input; approve appropriate source storage before archive ingestion.

Each task saves prompt.txt, source-manifest.json (paths, byte counts, SHA-256 hashes), response.json, and result.json. Image assignments are marked completed only when the response is valid JSON with the expected image path and a messages array containing each message's visible text and author. Extra extraction fields are discarded. Incomplete model answers are failures, not completed analyses. Each result identifies its assignment and source commit. Credentials are sent in a header and excluded from stored prompts and results.

Actions uploads separate task artifacts plus parallel-gemini-collected, whose index.json lists every planned assignment, including failed or missing results. A task failure retains successful neighbors. The collection is an outcome index, not a semantic synthesis or proof of analysis quality. Artifacts expire after 30 days; preserve selected long-term results separately when needed.

Run focused checks with python parallel-gemini/test_run_task.py. These cover assignment boundaries, source manifests, safe diagnostics, API behavior, incomplete responses, plan validation, and overlapping independent workers with isolated outputs. Mocked tests do not establish live Gemini behavior.

Choose meaningful work units and common context before using this substrate for the large archive. Chunking, evidence review, coverage, and final synthesis remain analysis-design tasks described above. The AGENTS Procedure governs the build and later analysis; the parallel workflow is the execution substrate for independent assignments.

# Stage 3 topic-guided sampling pilot

## Goal and result

Use the completed TF-IDF/NMF run and merged catalog to inspect representative source windows, identify question/context types, and produce the initial analysis matrix and shared output conventions. This completes an initial, explicitly sampled inspection milestone, not the whole Stage 3 analysis design or the final label catalog.

Inputs: [four-partition run](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/actions/runs/39028648832), [merger run](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/actions/runs/39028957505), and the merger's 54-topic catalog / source-referenced assignments. The merger covered 134 files, 1,334 conversations and 27,283 prepared document windows; these are computational coverage counts, not counts of semantically read conversations.

## Sampling method

Judgment sample of eight candidate topics (0, 7, 11, 21, 37, 43, 49, 53), chosen for varied question/context types and to include the filler-dominated cluster. For each, select its first saved representative document, reopen the exact source bin/record/node, and inspect the target, up to three ancestor nodes and one direct child on that branch. Eight bounded windows from eight distinct conversations were read; the complete conversations were not read. This is neither random nor prevalence-estimating. Topic representatives can favor short, lexically concentrated messages and are not guaranteed semantically typical.

The [sampling record](sampling-record.json) preserves target references, inspected context node IDs, conversation titles, candidate descriptions, and evidence limitations. No raw source messages are copied here. Parent links establish ancestry; alternate branches are not concatenated.

These observations concern the inspected source windows only. They do not validate the entire topic group, external facts, technical recommendations, legal statements, or practical outcomes.

command.instruction:
Standing Instructions for Conversation Archive Analysis Workers:
1. Supervisory Role vs. Worker Role: The Gemini supervisor designs, assigns, coordinates, and evaluates. Workers perform substantive technical execution, extraction, analysis, and verification. Do not return management summaries or unverified claims.
2. Traceable Citations and Grounding: Ground all findings and extracted data in explicit source references: source file path, conversation ID, mapping node ID, and message ID. Do not fabricate or generalize without citations.
3. Distinct Analytical Perspectives: Strictly distinguish user statements, assistant outputs, direct quotes from third parties, and user reports about others. Never conflate user descriptions of other people with those individuals' internal motives or verified actions.
4. No Clinical Diagnoses: Do not diagnose any person or treat diagnostic labels as established clinical facts. Track the provenance and context of any diagnostic terms without endorsing them.
5. Explicit Limits and Missing Sources: Attachment payloads in this export are absent; note this limitation rather than assuming contents. Explicitly state that current October 2026 data is absent from the August 2024–August 2026 archive rather than fabricating a contemporary comparison.
6. Nonce Consistency: Choose a unique worker nonce on your first return and reuse the exact same nonce on every subsequent response.
7. Output Delivery: When writing or updating files, place them in the issue workspace with clear file paths, descriptions, and provenance.

# Stage 3 topic-guided sampling pilot

## Goal and result

Use the completed TF-IDF/NMF run and merged catalog to inspect representative source windows, identify question/context types, and produce the initial analysis matrix and shared output conventions. This completes an initial, explicitly sampled inspection milestone, not the whole Stage 3 analysis design or the final label catalog.

Inputs: [four-partition run](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/actions/runs/39028648832), [merger run](https://github.com/BestNameYet/StateMachines/actions/runs/39028957505), and the merger's 54-topic catalog / source-referenced assignments. The merger covered 134 files, 1,334 conversations and 27,283 prepared document windows; these are computational coverage counts, not counts of semantically read conversations.

## Sampling method

Judgment sample of eight candidate topics (0, 7, 11, 21, 37, 43, 49, 53), chosen for varied question/context types and to include the filler-dominated cluster. For each, select its first saved representative document, reopen the exact source bin/record/node, and inspect the target, up to three ancestor nodes and one direct child on that branch. Eight bounded windows from eight distinct conversations were read; the complete conversations were not read. This is neither random nor prevalence-estimating. Topic representatives can favor short, lexically concentrated messages and are not guaranteed semantically typical.

The [sampling record](sampling-record.json) preserves target references, inspected context node IDs, conversation titles, candidate descriptions, and evidence limitations. No raw source messages are copied here. Parent links establish ancestry; alternate branches are not concatenated.

## Observed question/context types

| Candidate topic | Source-window observation | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | User questions why generated space-force commanders are aliens rather than humans. | Filler words do not identify a substantive topic; do not label this relationship material. |
| 7 | User distinguishes two resonator/flow mechanisms after a compactness/noise request. | Technical clarification needs preceding design constraints. |
| 11 | User corrects a shopping-list assumption about mounted thermometers. | Track operational constraints and corrections separately from broad food topics. |
| 21 | Hardware/cart advice for a tarp enclosure follows a message with no text. | Missing image payload limits verification of the assistant's visual claims. |
| 37 | User requests another source for an assistant-cited birth-record rule. | Separate source-checking behavior from truth of the legal claims. |
| 43 | User asks for a constraint-bound sprint-plan artifact and clarifies inputs/outputs. | Distinguish procedural model design from claims about official Scrum. |
| 49 | User removes unsupported offerings from business-profile copy. | Same food business can have a distinct marketing/copy-editing purpose. |
| 53 | Application-letter revisions mix employment goals and interpersonal context. | Preserve user reports versus assistant-authored draft text; no hiring outcome is established. |

These observations concern the inspected source windows only. They do not validate the entire topic group, external facts, technical recommendations, legal statements, or practical outcomes.

## Concrete outputs

- [Candidate topic index](candidate-topic-index.json): all 54 merged groups with keywords, model provenance and original representative references. All are marked provisional; it is a retrieval aid.
- [Sampling record](sampling-record.json): eight reviewed windows with source references.
- [Analysis matrix](analysis-matrix.json): five proposed questions, material, subjects/perspectives, methods, evidence requirements, coverage, limitations, intended outputs and next prompts. Priority is proposed, not user-approved.
- [Output conventions](output-conventions.json): separate topic/purpose/perspective/outcome dimensions, attribution, source references, ambiguity, branch handling and overlap rules.

## Remaining work

Expand sampling across date/length/branch strata and diverse model-score levels; audit more merged-topic members and contradictory examples; validate necessary field paths and explicit retention decisions; prioritize questions with the user; define exchange-based targets/context; compare passage sizes on the same conversations; inspect topic stability and mixed subjects before final catalog consolidation. The current message-window model is a retrieval pilot, not a validated classification-passage design.

Source originals are unchanged. Nothing here authorizes dropping unlisted keys or treating repeated assistant assertions as independent evidence.

state.standingInstructions:
Standing Instructions for Conversation Archive Analysis Workers:
1. Supervisory Role vs. Worker Role: The Gemini supervisor designs, assigns, coordinates, and evaluates. Workers perform substantive technical execution, extraction, analysis, and verification. Do not return management summaries or unverified claims.
2. Traceable Citations and Grounding: Ground all findings and extracted data in explicit source references: source file path, conversation ID, mapping node ID, and message ID. Do not fabricate or generalize without citations.
3. Distinct Analytical Perspectives: Strictly distinguish user statements, assistant outputs, direct quotes from third parties, and user reports about others. Never conflate user descriptions of other people with those individuals' internal motives or verified actions.
4. No Clinical Diagnoses: Do not diagnose any person or treat diagnostic labels as established clinical facts. Track the provenance and context of any diagnostic terms without endorsing them.
5. Explicit Limits and Missing Sources: Attachment payloads in this export are absent; note this limitation rather than assuming contents. Explicitly state that current October 2026 data is absent from the August 2024–August 2026 archive rather than fabricating a contemporary comparison.
6. Nonce Consistency: Choose a unique worker nonce on your first return and reuse the exact same nonce on every subsequent response.
7. Output Delivery: When writing or updating files, place them in the issue workspace with clear file paths, descriptions, and provenance.

values.matrixSummary: The refined Stage 3 analysis matrix establishes a rigorous, evidence-grounded framework across five distinct analytical questions (Q1 to Q5) and four non-overlapping analytical perspectives: the User, People Discussed, Interactions, and ChatGPT. Rather than conflating conversation text into generic summaries, each question operates with explicit methodological boundaries: Q1 focuses on user goals and unfinished technical/creative projects outside relationship topics; Q2 examines turn-by-turn user directives and assistant adaptations; Q3 isolates assistant-introduced premises, hallucinations, and unverified assumptions to prevent model echo; Q4 reconstructs the chronological evolution of ChatGPT usage across three verified operational periods spanning August 25, 2024 through August 5, 2026, while explicitly identifying the post-August 5, 2026 to October 2026 boundary gap; and Q5 addresses interpersonal interactions using a strict four-layer provenance model (direct third-party quotes, user event reports, user subjective reactions, and assistant diagnostic interpretations) that categorically prohibits clinical diagnosis and treats diagnostic labels (such as BPD) strictly as reported narrative terms with traceable provenance.

values.designSummary: The Stage 3 passage boundary specification establishes a four-tier structural hierarchy: Conversation -> Branch Path -> Ordered Turn Exchange -> Classification Passage. Natural conversation trees are decomposed into distinct, non-concatenated branch paths by following explicit parent-child pointer chains in the conversation mapping graph. Each branch path is partitioned into discrete turn exchanges (User prompt -> Assistant response, capturing intermediate tool operations). To ensure interpretive clarity without label contamination, every classification passage strictly delineates the active target exchange (the sole locus of label assignment and evidentiary quotation) from contextual framing (`contextBefore` for antecedent constraints and pronoun resolution; `contextAfter` for subsequent user corrections and reaction tracking). Overlap between sliding windows is tracked deterministically through explicit target node identifiers, preventing repeated context turns from inflating empirical evidence counts during synthesis.

boundaryRules.exchangeDefinition: An exchange unit is an ordered bipartite or tripartite turn sequence within an isolated conversation branch: commencing with a user prompt node (`message.author.role == 'user'`), traversing any immediate tool invocation or system intermediary nodes, and terminating at the corresponding assistant response node (`message.author.role == 'assistant'`). Null-message structural nodes are bypassed by following direct edge pointers.
boundaryRules.targetDelineation: The target passage is the primary evaluative unit consisting strictly of the designated core exchange. Semantic labels (subject/topic, user purpose, analytical perspective, conversation outcome) must be assigned solely based on text within the target passage. All label-supporting citations must reference message IDs, node IDs, and character offsets located exclusively within this target boundary.
boundaryRules.contextBeforeRules: Preceding context (`contextBefore`) encompasses up to N antecedent exchanges along the exact directed ancestry chain (`node.parent`). It provides necessary referential grounding, pronoun resolution, and background constraint awareness. Topics, requests, or entities appearing exclusively within `contextBefore` must not contribute labels or primary evidence counts to the target unit.
boundaryRules.contextAfterRules: Subsequent context (`contextAfter`) encompasses up to M descendant exchanges following the target's terminal node along the designated active branch. It provides visibility into user reactions, corrections, or follow-ups to evaluate conversation outcomes. Post-target shifts or subsequent inquiries occurring in `contextAfter` must never back-propagate to label the target unit.
boundaryRules.branchPreservationRules: Conversation tree structures must be traversed from root to leaf via parent-to-child links. Every fork point (`children.length > 1`) generates distinct, isolated branch paths. Alternative sibling replies are never concatenated or interleaved into a synthetic linear sequence. Each branch path maintains its own independent exchange sequence indexed by branch and node ancestry.
boundaryRules.overlapTrackingMechanism: Each prepared passage is indexed by a deterministic composite key (`targetPassageId`) and explicitly lists its constituent `targetNodeIds` separately from `contextNodeIds`. Evidence indexing, topic frequency aggregations, and perspective synthesis algorithms must filter strictly on `targetNodeIds`, ensuring that passages sharing context windows never produce duplicate evidentiary weight.

values.designSummary: The Stage 3 passage boundary specification establishes a four-tier structural hierarchy: Conversation -> Branch Path -> Ordered Turn Exchange -> Classification Passage. Natural conversation trees are decomposed into distinct, non-concatenated branch paths by following explicit parent-child pointer chains in the conversation mapping graph. Each branch path is partitioned into discrete turn exchanges (User prompt -> Assistant response, capturing intermediate tool operations). To ensure interpretive clarity without label contamination, every classification passage strictly delineates the active target exchange (the sole locus of label assignment and evidentiary quotation) from contextual framing (`contextBefore` for antecedent constraints and pronoun resolution; `contextAfter` for subsequent user corrections and reaction tracking). Overlap between sliding windows is tracked deterministically through explicit target node identifiers, preventing repeated context turns from inflating empirical evidence counts during synthesis.

boundaryRules.exchangeDefinition: An exchange unit is an ordered bipartite or tripartite turn sequence within an isolated conversation branch: commencing with a user prompt node (`message.author.role == 'user'`), traversing any immediate tool invocation or system intermediary nodes, and terminating at the corresponding assistant response node (`message.author.role == 'assistant'`). Null-message structural nodes are bypassed by following direct edge pointers.
boundaryRules.targetDelineation: The target passage is the primary evaluative unit consisting strictly of the designated core exchange. Semantic labels (subject/topic, user purpose, analytical perspective, conversation outcome) must be assigned solely based on text within the target passage. All label-supporting citations must reference message IDs, node IDs, and character offsets located exclusively within this target boundary.
boundaryRules.contextBeforeRules: Preceding context (`contextBefore`) encompasses up to N antecedent exchanges along the exact directed ancestry chain (`node.parent`). It provides necessary referential grounding, pronoun resolution, and background constraint awareness. Topics, requests, or entities appearing exclusively within `contextBefore` must not contribute labels or primary evidence counts to the target unit.
boundaryRules.contextAfterRules: Subsequent context (`contextAfter`) encompasses up to M descendant exchanges following the target's terminal node along the designated active branch. It provides visibility into user reactions, corrections, or follow-ups to evaluate conversation outcomes. Post-target shifts or subsequent inquiries occurring in `contextAfter` must never back-propagate to label the target unit.
boundaryRules.branchPreservationRules: Conversation tree structures must be traversed from root to leaf via parent-to-child links. Every fork point (`children.length > 1`) generates distinct, isolated branch paths. Alternative sibling replies are never concatenated or interleaved into a synthetic linear sequence. Each branch path maintains its own independent exchange sequence indexed by branch and node ancestry.
boundaryRules.overlapTrackingMechanism: Each prepared passage is indexed by a deterministic composite key (`targetPassageId`) and explicitly lists its constituent `targetNodeIds` separately from `contextNodeIds`. Evidence indexing, topic frequency aggregations, and perspective synthesis algorithms must filter strictly on `targetNodeIds`, ensuring that passages sharing context windows never produce duplicate evidentiary weight.

candidateModels.sizeWindow: 1 User Prompt + 1 Assistant Response (typically 200–800 tokens; 2 conversational turns)
candidateModels.rationale: Isolates the immediate functional request and response to measure whether topic discovery and classification can operate at minimal conversational granularity without noise from adjacent topics.
candidateModels.advantages: Eliminates intra-passage topic mixing; provides pinpoint citation accuracy and unambiguous speaker attribution; creates clean mapping boundaries that prevent adjacent discussion drift.
candidateModels.potentialRisks: Higher vulnerability to contextual insufficiency on short, elliptic, or anaphoric follow-up prompts (e.g., 'why?', 'continue', or pronoun-heavy responses), requiring frequent fallback to contextBefore.

candidateModels.sizeWindow: 3 Sequential Exchanges: Target centered between 1 preceding and 1 succeeding exchange (~1,200–3,500 tokens; 6 conversational turns)
candidateModels.rationale: Balances immediate request-reply mechanics with local conversational momentum, capturing immediate clarifications, corrections, and multi-turn explanations within a manageable context window.
candidateModels.advantages: High contextual sufficiency for iterative tasks, software debugging, and multi-step reasoning; directly captures correction loops (Q2) and immediate assistant assumptions (Q3) in a unified window.
candidateModels.potentialRisks: Moderate risk of topic mixing across abrupt conversational pivots; requires strict enforcement to ensure workers do not label background turns as target evidence.

candidateModels.sizeWindow: Variable Window of 5 to 10 Sequential Exchanges bounded by detected topic shifts or session pauses (up to 8,000 tokens; 10–20 turns)
candidateModels.rationale: Evaluates whether macro-level user trajectories, protracted project designs, or extended relationship reflections can be captured holistically as unified episodes.
candidateModels.advantages: Maximizes contextual sufficiency and thematic coherence for long-horizon goals (Q1) and chronological usage analysis (Q4); avoids artificial fragmentation of extended workflows.
candidateModels.potentialRisks: Severe topic dilution and keyword mixing; citations become coarse or ambiguous across long transcripts; high risk of conflating distinct conversational shifts into a single generic label.
